event.text: Why is the sky blue? Answer in one sentence.
Sunlight scatters off air molecules, and shorter blue wavelengths scatter far more than red, so blue reaches our eyes from all directions.
And why are sunsets red? One sentence.
Sunsets look red because at low angles sunlight passes through much more air, which scatters away most of the blue and green light and leaves the longer red wavelengths to reach your eyes.
